text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Monday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- According to the central election committee, the turnout at the local elections in Riga was 49.58 percent. Preliminary results of the election will be announced later today.
- The Polish interior ministry blames the attack of the Latvian bus in Poland, in which one passenger was killed, on criminals from the CIS.
- Most Riga residents polled by Diena said they voted for the Social Democrats and parties which have not yet been in power as yet.
- By March 5, the state budget deficit was 1.91 million lats, normal at the beginning of each month.

- Meeting with the press on Sunday, President Ulmanis said he is afraid that Latvia may not be admitted to NATO and should therefore lay more stress on joining the European Union. Ulmanis pledged that he will discuss the issue while meeting with foreign leaders this week.
- Latvian Foreign Minister Valdis Birkavs announced that Latvia's plans to consolidate its eastern border, which should one day become the eastern border of the EU.
- Parliament heads from Latvia, Estonia and Lithuania will meet on March 14 in the Lithuanian coastal town of Palanga.
- The government is to formulate its stand on state monopolies in the sectors of telecommunications and insurance by the middle of March to make it possible for Latvia to join the WTO.
- The government has ordered the law on the free port of Ventspils to be amended.
- Inflation in February ran at 0.4 percent, which is the lowest indicator among the Baltic states.
- EU Minister Aleksandrs Kirshteins said that over the next few years to come Latvia is likely to get $4 billion in foreign investment.
- According to official statistics, timber was Latvia's largest export in 1996. Of total exports worth 795 million lats, timber made up 211.2 million lats.
